_meta.completeness: COMPLETE — All 7 steps of Accela Building Permit Pre-Application flow fully documented from live portal walkthrough. All PDF forms cataloged. JSON is ready for Phase 5 and Phase 6 development.
forms_that_are_upload_only_not_fillable: Architectural Plans (Floor Plan, Elevations, Sections, etc.) — architect draws these
Structural Plans + Calculations — structural engineer draws these
Title 24 Energy Compliance Report — Title 24 consultant prepares this
CALGreen GB-1 Sheet — architect/green building consultant prepares this
Geotechnical Report — geotechnical engineer prepares this
Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP) — civil engineer draws this
T-1 Tree Protection Sheet — landscape architect or arborist draws this
Electrical / Mechanical / Plumbing Plans — trade contractors draw these
still_not_researchable_by_ai: Accela portal online fields — requires manual walkthrough with a real account at aca-prod.accela.com/PALOALTO. Create account, start fake ADU permit, screenshot every screen.
key_architecture_notes: Palo Alto uses ONE combined Building Permit Application PDF for all trades. No separate electrical/plumbing/mechanical forms.
The Utility Service Application is submitted to the Utilities Dept SEPARATELY from the Building Permit. Submit both simultaneously.
CRITICAL: Palo Alto only allows ONE utility service per lot. Separately-metered ADU requires a dual-meter panel. Surface to homeowner during intake.
Special Inspection Agreement is NOT required at submittal — only required before permit ISSUANCE.
Smoke/CO Certification is submitted to the building inspector at final inspection, not at submittal.
_meta.master_adu_filing_note: All Master ADU applications filed under 250 Hamilton Avenue in Accela, not the project address
_meta.applicable_codes: 2025 California Building Standards Code, PAMC Chapter 15.04 & Chapter 16

utility_service_application.form_name: Utility Service Application — Permanent Single Family Residential
utility_service_application.submitted_to: Utilities Dept — SEPARATELY from building permit. Submit simultaneously to avoid delays.
utility_service_application.timing_warning: Electric review takes up to 45 business days. Permanent installation takes 30-40 more business days after payment. Start this early.
utility_service_application.critical_rule: Palo Alto allows only ONE utility service per lot. Separately-metered ADU = contractor installs dual-meter panel on main house.

sb407_plumbing_compliance.form_name: Plumbing Fixture Replacement Certificate of Compliance (SB 407)
sb407_plumbing_compliance.submitted_to: Building inspector at FINAL inspection — permit cannot be finaled without signed copy
sb407_plumbing_compliance.key_shortcut: If Regrid yearbuilt > 1994 → entire form is auto-exempt. Just needs owner signature on Q4 line. Very common for newer Palo Alto homes.

ai_fillable.label: Q1: Registered historical site?
ai_fillable.source: cross-reference Palo Alto Historic Resources list; default false

ai_fillable.label: Q4: Built on or before January 1, 1994?
ai_fillable.source: Regrid props.yearbuilt — yearbuilt > 1994 → No → form exempt
ai_fillable.notes: yearbuilt > 1994 = full exemption. No fixture inventory needed.

ai_fillable.label: Property Type: Single-Family
ai_fillable.source: SFR + ADU = single-family for SB-407 per Palo Alto policy

human_required.label: Q2: Licensed plumber certifies installation not feasible?
human_required.hint: Almost always No.

human_required.label: Q3: Water service permanently disconnected?
human_required.hint: Almost always No.

human_required.label: Owner certifies all non-compliant fixtures replaced
human_required.hint: For pre-1994 homes: certify all toilets (>1.6 gpf), showerheads (>2.5 gpm), and faucets (>2.2 gpm) have been upgraded. Your plumber can verify.

ai_fillable.label: New Living Area (SF)
ai_fillable.source: ADU or addition SF from scope

human_required.label: Construction Type
human_required.hint: Almost all Palo Alto residential ADUs are Type V-B. Confirm with your architect.

special_inspection_agreement.when_required: Required BEFORE PERMIT ISSUANCE (not at submittal) for projects requiring special inspection per CBC Section 1701
special_inspection_agreement.notes: Two parts: (1) agreement page with signatures, (2) structural inspection schedule checklist. The checklist is filled by the structural engineer — AI cannot determine which inspection types apply without the structural drawings. Chosen should treat the checklist as upload-only / architect-fills.

human_required.label: Name of Special Inspection Agency
human_required.hint: Select a City of Palo Alto approved inspection agency. A list of approved agencies with contact info and expiration dates is included in the form (pages 3-4). Recommended: ACEQuality Control, Applied Materials & Engineering, Consolidated Engineering Labs, or Testing Engineers Inc.

human_required.label: Structural Tests and Inspection Schedule — which inspection types apply
human_required.hint: This is a detailed checklist (reinforcing steel, concrete, structural steel, wood, etc.) that your structural engineer fills based on the structural drawings. AI cannot determine this. Architect/engineer provides this.

green_building_inspection_agreement.form_name: Green Building Special Inspector Inspection Agreement
green_building_inspection_agreement.submitted_to: Building Dept with permit application — required BEFORE PERMIT ISSUANCE
green_building_inspection_agreement.when_required: All new ADUs and additions — CALGreen compliance is mandatory
green_building_inspection_agreement.notes: Simpler than the structural inspection agreement. AI can fill most fields and auto-select the correct CALGreen tier.

ai_fillable.label: Select Applicable Project Requirements — CALGreen Tier
ai_fillable.source: Residential CALGreen Mandatory Plus Tier 2 — ALWAYS checked for new detached ADU and new SFR per master-adu-checklist-2026 requirement
ai_fillable.notes: This is deterministic: new detached ADU always = Tier 2. No human input needed.

human_required.label: Special Inspection Agency Name (Green Building)
human_required.hint: Can be the same agency as your structural special inspector, or a separate green building inspector. Must be qualified for green building inspections.

smoke_co_alarm_certification.form_name: Self-Certification for Smoke Detectors & Carbon Monoxide Alarms
smoke_co_alarm_certification.submitted_to: Building inspector — presented at final inspection
smoke_co_alarm_certification.when_required: Any work exceeding $1,000 that requires a permit. Applies to all ADU projects.
smoke_co_alarm_certification.notes: Extremely simple form. Certifies that smoke and CO alarms are installed per code. Nearly 100% AI-fillable — only requires a wet signature from licensed contractor or property owner.

smoke_alarms: Outside sleeping area in immediate vicinity
co_alarms: In bedroom where fuel-burning appliance is located
requirements_summary.palo_alto_specific: Smoke alarms must be photoelectric type (or equivalent). Replace every 10 years.

ai_fillable.label: I am the: Licensed Contractor / Property Owner
ai_fillable.source: If contractor signs → Licensed Contractor. If homeowner signs → Property Owner.

human_required.label: Signature and Date
human_required.hint: Sign and date to certify that smoke alarms and CO alarms have been installed in every required location and tested. Signed by contractor or property owner.
human_required.who_answers: contractor or homeowner (wet signature or e-signature)

submission_sequence: 1. SIMULTANEOUSLY: Submit building permit package to Accela + utility service application to Utilities Dept
2. BEFORE PERMIT ISSUANCE: Submit Special Inspection Agreement + Green Building Agreement
3. AT FINAL INSPECTION: Submit SB-407 (signed) + Smoke/CO Certification (signed)
4. AFTER ACCELA ASSIGNS PERMIT NUMBER: Fill permit_number field on utility application and all inspection forms

accela_pre_application_step5.form_name: Accela Building Permit Pre-Application — Step 5: Documents
accela_pre_application_step5.notes: FREE-FORM upload at pre-application stage. No specific required documents listed. Just upload plans or supporting docs in PDF format. The full document checklist (architectural plans, structural plans, Title 24, etc.) is required at the actual building permit submission, NOT at pre-application.

upload_requirements.what_to_upload_at_preapp: Preliminary plans, sketches, or any supporting documents that help city staff understand the project scope. Not required to be complete.

accela_pre_application_step5.phase5_implication: Chosen should provide a simple drag-and-drop upload area at pre-application stage. Label it: Upload preliminary plans or project description (PDF, optional at this stage).

accela_pre_application_step6_7.notes: Step 6 shows a full review of all entered data with Edit buttons for each section. Step 7 is the final submission with a certification checkbox.
